title: Descent of the tensor-route equality from K-flat models
statement: For the same explicit ordinary monoidal pullback data, an equality of the residue tensor-route and tensor-model maps on every homotopy complex whose ordinary pullback is K-flat descends, by naturality and essential surjectivity of the derived quotient, to the equality on every homotopy complex.

proof.text: Package tensorModelTarget as a natural transformation: use inverse braiding, tensor the fixed coefficient counit with the variable exact-pullback counit, then apply the lax tensor map of Qh. Package tensorModelMapWith as the composite of the tensor-presentation counit, the exact-pullback counit, the homotopy single-tensor comparison, and the ordinary oplax comparison. Their components are exactly the two maps in the statement.

The kFlatMap left derivability structure gives, for the given homotopy complex P, a left resolution w : R -> P with R in kFlatMap and w a quasi-isomorphism. Apply the hypothesis to R. The map Qh(w) is invertible.

Naturality of the two transformations along w identifies their components at P after precomposition by (H composed with derived pullback)(Qh(w)). This morphism is invertible because Qh(w) is invertible. Cancel it and identify the components with the stated route and model maps. This uses a homotopy resolution arrow, so it does not require the ordinary tensor-model target to factor through the derived category.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.5.9(3), Remark 6.8.15; naturality and K-flat resolution descent
proof_origin.note: The complete Lean proof constructs the two natural transformations and cancels the derived image of an actual quasi-isomorphism R -> P. It does not transport the ordinary tensor-model target along an arbitrary derived isomorphism.
